mathematical_reason: ProofWiki presents both fraction representations and the more structural field-of-fractions definition. Fractions are equivalence classes of integer numerator/denominator pairs, so p/q is not a unique syntactic representation. This definition is independent of the construction of R and useful for rational Cauchy sequences. The representation equality criterion can be established within Z.

The separately sourced Rational Sequence entry specifies rational codomain and the general Sequence entry specifies an index set drawn from N. We must not confuse a rational sequence with a rational-number-valued limit, and finite sequences are not the ones used in the classical rational-Cauchy completion.

ProofWiki defines absolute value in any ordered integral domain and explicitly lists Q as an instance. Applying the order-based definition to Q remains entirely rational-valued; it must not be replaced by the square-root model for general real numbers. Rational epsilon and rational differences can thus be compared without circularity.

ProofWiki distinguishes Q_{>0} from its use of 'positive rational number' for Q_{≥0}, which includes zero. Quantifiers in the Cauchy criterion must use strictly positive rational epsilon. The two conventions cannot be conflated or grouped under the same uncontrolled 'positive' variant.
